window.frame: pushes r15/r14/r13/r12/rbp/rbx, 0x68-byte stack adjustment, canary fs:0x28 at rsp+0x58, checked on every return path
window.note: single FDE; the next FDE starts at 0x542fe90. The throw/length_error paths inside the range are part of this FDE; the window has no landing pads of its own.

arguments.out: rdi: pointer to a std::string that receives the result; the function returns the same pointer
arguments.status: rsi: pointer to a status record: code u8 at +0, subcode u8 at +1, message C-string pointer (nullable) at +8
arguments.not_read: status bytes +2..+7 are never read by this function; their roles are not claimed
arguments.returns: the out string pointer (rbx in rax on return)

code_table.note: code 0 writes 'OK' directly into the out string and returns; subcode and message are ignored

jump_table.entry_type: int32 offset relative to the table base
jump_table.dispatch: code > 15 skips the table and takes the unknown-code fallback; code <= 15 jumps through table[code]

unknown_fallback.call: __snprintf_chk into a 30-byte stack buffer (29 characters plus NUL); the code byte is the %d argument
unknown_fallback.note: the longest rendering, 'Unknown code(255): ', is 19 characters, so the 30-byte buffer always fits; the fallback prefix then joins the same subcode/message flow as the known codes

subcode_table.entry_type: one qword per subcode; file bytes read zero in this capture, values come from R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations (see relocations.txt)

entries.name: Failed to acquire lock due to max_num_locks limit

assembly_rules: code 0: out is set to 'OK' and the function returns; subcode and message are never read on this path
code 1..15, or the unknown-code fallback: out starts as the code prefix (or the fallback rendering)
subcode == 0: if the message pointer is non-null, the message is appended directly after the prefix
subcode != 0: the subcode name is appended after the prefix; if the message pointer is non-null, ': ' is appended, then the message
message == null: the result ends after the prefix (plus the subcode name when subcode != 0); no separator is appended
every append checks the remaining room against 0x3fffffffffffffff and throws length_error past it (recorded, not modeled as output)
the finished local string is move-assigned into out: the SSO path copies the bytes, the heap path transfers the buffer pointer; the observable string is identical either way
prefixes of length <= 15 are built in the local string's inline buffer; longer prefixes go through _M_create first; the boundary is an implementation detail, the output string is the same

callers.census_method: full executable-segment e8/e9 scans for target 0x542f8a0 plus a whole-file qword scan; the full site list with enclosing FDEs is in callers.tsv (regenerated by gen_callers.py)
callers.replay_loop_site: 0x520b5e2 in 0x520ad30..0x520c053 (excerpted in caller-replay.txt): the WAL replay loop builds a Corruption status for a too-small record with the detail builder 0x542f040, formats it here, and logs '[WalManager] %s%s: dropping %d bytes; %s'
callers.note: the census is a call-site list only; the behavior of the other 177 callers is not claimed

consumers.detail_builder: 0x542f040 fills the status record this formatter reads (code at +0, subcode at +1, message buffer at +8); the replay loop's use passes code 2, subcode 0, message 'log record too small'

unknowns: subcode values above 15: the table holds exactly 16 entries, so the binary would read past it; that behavior is not pinned and the model rejects subcode > 15
status bytes +2..+7: never read here; their meaning (if any) belongs to the status record's owner, not to this formatter
the internals of _M_append/_M_create beyond the append contract used here (append bytes, length cap, length_error past the cap)
not_claimed: the behavior of any caller other than the replay-loop site above

any first-party-versus-library judgement beyond the pinned bytes: the code/subcode tables are RocksDB's Status vocabulary as retained in node #94, and the formatter is mapped as an RE-001 function-map item because the WAL manager consumes it
